text: The rocks lay smooth and silver by the shore.
Sunny climbed to watch the evening sea.
Upon the rocks she heard a happy bark,
and found a roly-poly ball of fur.
A seal pup! Round and soft with great dark eyes,
and whiskers dripping diamonds from his swim.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “Did you swim all day?”
“All day!” he barked. “The sea's my playground!”
He showed her how he rolled upon the rocks,
and clapped his little flippers with a laugh.
But rolling makes a little pup grow tired,
and soon his happy barking turned to yawns.
“The waves will sing to us,” he said, “all night.
The sea's the best at singing lullabies.”
So Sunny listened to the ocean's song,
the hush and shush of water on the stones.
The seal pup snuggled down upon his rock,
still warm from all the sunshine of the day.
He tucked his flippers close against his sides,
a sleepy silver pebble on the shore.
Sunny found a sandy sheltered spot,
and curled up to the rhythm of the waves.
The shore was still, except the singing sea.
Everything was peaceful, soft, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy with the ocean's song.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the sleeping pup,
both rocked to dreams by lullabies of waves.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little seal pup.
Goodnight, singing sea. Goodnight, little one.
